problem: Prior image-imagination VLN work (HAMT/DUET-Imagine, PanoGen) works on discrete panoramas and only imagines goals, with no online action-conditioned prediction or explicit planning value. Other world-model methods replace the planner with long-horizon rollout objectives that are brittle and slow, and VLM-only scoring favors salient but unreachable targets.
motivation: Language-vision matching says what looks relevant but not whether it is reachable, so it can't foresee occlusions or collisions and causes detours. Long rollouts accumulate pose and appearance drift and limit how many candidates can be evaluated. The paper's observation is that short-horizon, action-conditioned imagination projected into map space can add reachability-aware guidance while leaving the planner intact.
key_idea: Roll out short-horizon, action-conditioned egocentric futures with a latent CDiT world model, convert them into an egocentric imagined value map, and fuse it with the frontier planner's native score at score level.
insight: Imagination is most useful as a map-space value used as a reachability-aware tie-breaker, not as a replacement planner. The paper's ablation goes VLFM to VISTA to VISTAv2 and shows the last step (imagination to value with fusion) gives the largest SPL gain and shorter trajectories (Val-Unseen SPL 68.3 to 73.7, TL 13.26 to 10.73). A naive long-horizon pixel-space NWM planner performed much worse because of drift. The uncertainty-gating sweep peaks at θ=0.6, so noisy rollouts must be gated. Note that the VLFM-to-VISTA comparison mixes different systems, so it is a weak causal test.
method: World model: a CDiT-L video diffusion model in VAE latent space (NWM encoder/decoder) that predicts H=4 egocentric future frames from the last m frames, the instruction embedding and per-step action tokens (Δx,Δy,sinΔθ,cosΔθ,κ with time code and turn/straight mode bit). It uses a distilled sampler and sparse decoding (every Δt frames).

Language reasoner and prior map: frozen BLIP text and image features give per-pixel alignment scores, which are depth-splatted onto the egocentric local map as an action-agnostic language prior V_prior.

Imagination-to-Value (I2V) head: each decoded imagined frame gets a confidence map, a learned non-negative combination of instruction alignment, traversability and an obstacle/uncertainty penalty. It is projected to an 80x80 grid over a 12 m window with depth-aware splatting and aggregated across rollouts by discounted log-sum-exp.

Score-level fusion: S_fused = S_base + λ1 Σ γ^τ V_img + λ2 Σ γ^τ V_prior over path samples. The top candidate is chosen and its first control executed in a receding-horizon loop, with the base frontier planner unchanged.
Uncertainty gating: rollout variance from an ensemble or diffusion is used to disable imagination with a hard threshold θ=0.6 when it is high.
Training: the world model is trained on 489k egocentric RGB frames with poses and actions from HM3D/MP3D, using 8x RTX 6000 Ada for about 8 days (~200k steps). Inference runs on a single RTX 4090.

numbers_note: Benchmark is called R2R in the paper but run as continuous VLN-CE in Habitat, hence R2R-CE. The RoboTHOR split is not stated, so 'val' is a guess. The paper says HM3D val was adopted but reports no HM3D results. The text says Val-Unseen SR is +3.6 over VISTA, but the ablation section says +1.6 (81.4 vs 77.8 gives 3.6).
results: On R2R Val-Unseen, VISTAv2 reaches 81.4 SR / 73.7 SPL with TL 10.73, beating VISTA (77.8/68.3) and PanoGen (74.2/64.3). NE is worse (3.76 vs 2.92). On Test-Unseen, SPL is 69.0 (best) but SR is 73.1, below VISTA's 74.9. On RoboTHOR it reaches 61.3 SR / 34.7 SWPL, against VISTA's 43.1/28.8 and ESC's 38.1/22.2.
limitations: Rollouts are short-horizon and depend on monocular depth and pose estimates. Failures occur on mirrors, glass and low-texture or cluttered scenes, where traversability is overestimated.
The policy sometimes stops just outside the 3 m radius, so SR falls and NE rises on Test-Unseen relative to VISTA.

No real-robot evaluation, and no per-component ablation of the I2V cues or the prior term. Comparisons mix different sensor and protocol setups, and the paper's own text is inconsistent about the SR gain.
